units.text: A kettle gone cold on the stove.
A phone propped against a bowl of fruit, its screen dark.
IRIS LENNOX, 30s, sits at the table in a cardigan, a mug between her hands, a letter folded beside it.
She unfolds the letter and reads the first line under her breath.
"Dear Iris. I have started this letter nine times."
units.name: IRIS

units.text: Then a flat electronic beep, no greeting at all.
That's a stupid way to start. You know it's me. You've always known.
units.name: IRIS

units.text: She laughs, once, and wipes her eye.
I got your letter. I read it standing up in the hallway because I couldn't make it to the kitchen. I read it four times. It's a very good letter. You always did write better than you talked.
units.name: IRIS

units.text: You said you were sorry. You said it three times, actually. I counted. Sorry for leaving. Sorry for the way you left. Sorry for the Thursday.
units.name: IRIS

units.text: Her thumb moves along the mug's rim.
I want to tell you I'm not angry. That would be easier. But I am a little. Not at you. At the Thursday. At whoever decided Thursday was a good day for a person to decide something like that.
units.name: IRIS

units.text: She sets the phone on the table, on speaker, and leans toward it.
You asked if I'd call. I said I wouldn't. I've been sitting here for forty minutes not calling. So.
units.name: IRIS

units.text: Here's what I wanted to say. I wanted to say that the dog is fine. He's fat. He misses you. He sits by the door at six. I know that's not fair to tell you but I'm telling you.
units.name: IRIS

units.text: And I wanted to say that I forgive you, but I'm not ready to say it out loud, so I'm saying it into a machine, which is a little like a church, if you think about it. Nobody answers but you feel lighter.
units.name: IRIS

units.text: I'm going to hang up now. Or you'll have to listen to all the rest. There's a lot of rest.
units.name: IRIS

units.text: She reaches for the screen, then pulls her hand back.
Daniel. Call me on Sunday. Or don't. But the porch light will be on.
units.name: IRIS

units.text: Slowly, deliberately, she gets up, goes to the window, and flicks on the porch light.
